the run, in order

A build is not one task. It is a dozen, spread over weeks.

So this is not a feature list — it is the run itself. Each step leaves an artifact on the record. The graphics below are illustrative compositions of the planned workspace, not live captures.

The run

01Discover 02Vet 03Plan 04Forge 05Deliver 06Prepare

Step 01Discover

It reads the live feed, so nothing current slips past.

Open opportunities straight from the source listings — filtered to open, ranked against your stack, with every fit claim pointing at the evidence it came from.

Feed
planned
Open listings, filtered and ranked against your stack and hours.
Fit
cited
Explainable fit with the claims it rests on — never a bare score.
Partial data
visible
A failed retrieval shows as a gap, never a confident guess.

Step 02Vet

It reads the fine print and pins every claim.

A rules page becomes an immutable snapshot, then verbatim claims — each citing the line it came from — and a fit verdict against your country, stack and hours.

Step 03Plan

One brief. Three documents. A review gate.

Versioned scope, PRD and spec for your actual idea — contest or no contest. Design approval binds to the exact revision, and a locked scope line flags anything that tries to grow.

Locked line: brief + repo + review

Cut→scheduler · push · auth · crawler

Step 04Forge

Specialists build in a sandbox. You hold the gates.

A coordinator delegates to restricted specialists building in an isolated sandbox. Review mode pauses at feature gates; production, destructive and default-branch actions always need your explicit approval. Three failed repairs on the same issue pause the run.

Sandbox
isolated
Generated code never runs on Caddie's own host or your machine.
Acceptance
machine-checked
Agent self-reports never count as success; command exits and browser proof do.
Repairs
bounded
Three failed attempts on the same issue pause for a human.

Step 05Deliver

Receipts, not vibes.

The verified patch lands as a feature-branch PR in your own GitHub — one logical PR per intent, operation receipts retained, never a force-push. Merging to a default branch is your call, explicitly.

Delivery
receipted
Unique operation keys; a retried intent reconciles instead of duplicating.
Force-push
never
Unrelated source files are preserved; conflicts come back reviewable.
Default branch
your call
Explicit owner approval at execution time — no exceptions.

Step 06Prepare

Then it stops, and the human presses Submit.

Judging against the contest's actual rubric, a submission package with missing fields honestly missing, and demo/live integrations labelled. Caddie prepares; it never submits.

Rubric
actual
Scores compare artifact evidence against the real criteria — not generic ones.
Missing fields
missing
No invented video links, no invented licenses, no win probabilities.
Submissions by Caddie
0

keep it honest

An AI that reads the rules can also misread them.

So the product is built around being checkable rather than around sounding confident.

evidence

Machine-checked, never self-reported

Success is a command exit and a browser assertion — never the agent's own account of the work.

freshness

Stamped with its age

Each card carries the time it last updated. Three hours old says three hours old.

re-check

Changes become deltas

The previous snapshot and source URL are retained, so a moved clause shows up as a delta you can see.

privacy

Your build stays yours

Projects, plans and artifacts are private to your account. Previews are private and expiring by default.

what caddie will not do

The club stays in your hands.

  • ✕It will not swing for you — the build, the demo and the pitch are yours.
  • ✕It will not spend, deploy or merge without your explicit approval; production, destructive and default-branch actions stay owner-gated at execution time.
  • ✕It will not call a rule it couldn't read "clear". A failed read shows up as unknown.

LOCKED LINE: APPROVED BOUNDARIES ONLY ▍
